title: You are not losing to better people.
lead: You are losing to people who are easier to find. That is a fixable problem, and it takes about an hour.
outcomes: A positioning line that could not sit on three hundred other profiles
Your headline and about section rewritten while we talk, not afterwards
A 90 day plan. Who to message. What to say. In what order.

process.title: Book
process.body: Pick a slot and pay. Two minutes. The card is the only filter.

process.title: I do the homework
process.body: I read your profile, your CV, and five real job posts for the role you named.

process.title: We work
process.body: Sixty minutes. Screen shared. We rewrite live. No slides.

process.title: You ship
process.body: You get the doc we wrote together, plus a checklist for the first 30 days.

forYou: You are a few years in and the next step is not obvious from where you stand
You want to move from a big company into a startup, or from doing the work into running it
You have a profile and never post. Or you post and nothing happens.
You would rather send ten precise messages than two hundred applications
You will do the homework between booking and the call
notForYouLabel: This is not for you if
notForYou: You want someone to apply to jobs for you
You want a guaranteed offer. Nobody can promise that. I will not pretend.
You are a company looking to hire. That is RallyUp, one click away.
You have not decided to change anything yet

faq.a: $100, paid when you book. One hour on Google Meet.
No. LinkedIn is where the work ends up. The work is deciding what you are for and who should care. The profile is the output.

faq.q: Will you write my posts for me?
faq.a: No. I do that for executives through RallyUp at a very different price. You leave this hour able to write your own.
Your CV. Your profile. A rough idea of the role you want. Two out of three is fine. Book anyway.

faq.q: What if it does not help?
faq.a: Email me within a week and I refund it. I would rather lose the fee than have you tell people it was a waste.

story: Two years ago I was a management consultant. High rise office, billion dollar clients, the whole picture of the thing I thought I wanted.
Nobody outside my team knew what I did. I was good at the work. I was invisible at the job.
Then at 23 I sent one cold message to a founder I had never met. He replied in thirty minutes. I am now his chief of staff.
Nothing about me changed in those thirty minutes. I did not get smarter. I got legible.

That is the whole gap. Being good at your job and being known for being good at your job are two separate projects. Most people only run the first one. Then they watch the role go to someone visibly worse.

I spend my working life fixing this for executives at Airwallex, PandaDoc and Letter.ai. They pay an agency a lot of money for it. You do not need an agency. You need one hour and someone who will not let you stay vague.
